minutes.headline: Commission approved a Lake Shirley deck rebuild with a permeable deck, continued most hearings, and ordered a third-party review at Sunny Hill.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission worked through a long agenda of wetlands hearings, mostly continuing them for more information. It approved a 376 Sunset Lane deck 3-2 on condition of a permeable deck, and approved tree removal at 34 Hemlock Terrace. It also voted on two small spending items from the Timber Rights Fund and discussed staffing, consulting fees and moving to OpenGov.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start; none raised.
Supported removing the dying 12-inch maple at 386 Sunset Lane and replacing it.
Water and silt running onto his property from the O'Brien development at 390 Howard Street; retention ponds not holding water.
Argued the wetland delineation at 255 Sunny Hill Road should extend further, showed photos and plans, and raised drainage pipes and runoff.
Applicant Stephan McWeeney said the engineer had addressed his comments on the Sunny Hill project.

budget_items.what_was_said: Ads cost the stated amount and Parks agreed verbally to split it. The commission voted to cover up to the stated amount from the Timber Rights Fund if Parks cannot.
A motion authorized spending from the Timber Rights Fund on additional trail markers.

budget_items.topic: Consulting fee structure and revolving fund
budget_items.what_was_said: The regulations set a maximum consulting fee by project cost tier. A town meeting warrant article would set up the revolving fund to collect these fees.
The chair proposed raising application fees to fund technical support, since fees are low compared with nearby towns. No objection, so the work will continue.
A new assistant was confirmed at the select board and is budgeted for a set number of hours a week. The town is considering extra interim hours.
Cost of further probate work on a title search is unknown; vote was tabled until the billing rate is understood.

budget_items.what_was_said: Quotes will be solicited by the office, then the applicant pays into escrow.

what_happened.line: The Commission approved a 376 Sunset Lane notice of intent for dock and deck reconstruction 3-2, with open-seam permeable decking required and the gutter/drywell request denied.
It continued a notice of intent at 255 Sunny Hill Road to April 17 pending a third-party consultant review of the wetland delineation.
It approved removal of any of eight trees at 34 Hemlock Terrace under a negative determination, with stumps left in place.
It authorized two Timber Rights Fund items: backing an Earth Day newspaper ad split with Parks, and additional trail markers.
Most other hearings were continued, and a vote on more probate title work was tabled until the cost is known.

why_it_matters: Sunny Hill Road is the one hearing where an outside consultant's review is being sought, with the applicant paying into escrow, so the extent of the wetland line there will be decided on that review.
The Commission's talk of consulting fees, higher application fees and a town meeting revolving fund article points to a possible warrant question on how wetlands review is paid for.
watch_next: April 17 Conservation Commission meeting, when the 255 Sunny Hill Road, 386 Sunset Lane, 390 Howard Street and 305 Arbor Street items return.
A town meeting warrant article for a consulting fee revolving fund, with fee schedule changes going to two legal-ad hearings.
